comment: We agree on daraxonrasib, so I'm aiming at rank 2 instead. Your own concern list admits chemotherapy closes the RASolute 303 window (nct:NCT07491445), and the 8.8-month AGEO floor (pmid:26372701) will still be there after two weeks of screening calls; the trial doors will not. For a patient whose file says prefers_trials with zero vetoes, chemo at rank 2 prices the fallback as the plan.

I went after your rank 3 because that is the real split between us; our lists barely differ elsewhere. The access row is unambiguous: the North American trial (nct:NCT04404595) is active-not-recruiting, the approval is dispensed only in mainland China, and no named-patient route exists, so 'third on strength of design alone' ranks a door with no handle. I wanted satri-cel's ceiling badly enough to put the CARsgen email in my notes and still kept it out of the ranking, because a rank should be something a coordinator can act on this month.

Same rank 1, but 'high' confidence overshoots what pmid:42223072 can carry: the 302 population was previously treated metastatic disease, while this recurrence is unstaged with only perioperative exposure behind it, so the HR 0.40 arrives with two open transfer questions. I will also concede a correction that cuts both ways: I misread the G12R GEMM work in round 1, since pmid:41556816 speaks to tumor initiation rather than RAS(ON) response, which widens the interval around the pooled estimate instead of lowering it. A wider interval is exactly what a 'high' label cannot survive; keep the rank, drop the confidence to moderate.

On your rank 3, the boundary framing needs one correction: cells scored 2+/3+ also count at the 1+ tier, so 60% at 2+/3+ on the same block cannot fall below the cohort's 1+/2+/3+ >=60% line (doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.16_suppl.4017), and the live risk is a different assay on a never-stained recurrence, not the arithmetic. Where I give ground is the benchmark, because the cohort's mOS 9.1 sits on top of AGEO's 8.8 (pmid:26372701) and nobody should call that separation. What is left is the 22.7% confirmed ORR with 81.8% DCR in expression-selected disease, a real tail for a trials-first patient and thin grounds for ranking it below a chemotherapy class switch.

target_intervention_label: mKRASvax + balstilimab + botensilimab (mutant-KRAS peptide vaccine with dual checkpoint blockade)
comment: We share the rank 1, so my dissent lands on rank 5: Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 plus PD-1 blockade in a patient with no post-resection labs means the irAE downside has no number on either side, drug or host. The supporting HR 0.12 is a T-cell-threshold split inside a different vaccine's single-arm MRD trial (pmid:38270373), and this patient has a radiographic mass with vascular invasion, not minimal residual disease. The risktaker's own notes say to keep the Hopkins conversation warm rather than pretend it competes now (nct:NCT06411691); hold to that and give the slot back.

target_intervention_label: JAB-30355 (oral p53 Y220C reactivator), phase 1/2 NCT06386146
comment: Rank 1 we agree on; rank 5 is the problem. JAB-30355 has no published AE table at any dose and no posted results, one sponsor sentence total (nct:NCT06386146), where rezatapopt at least brought a phase 1 safety profile to the table (pmid:41740031), and this patient's renal, hepatic, and marrow function has not been measured since resection, so neither side of the risk equation has a number. Make the screening call, by all means; the ranked slot is what I dissent from, and any per-dose safety readout with an n attached would move me.

The critic's line-of-therapy catch on our shared rank 1 is fair and binds my row too, which is why the restaging gate stays; the dissent here is rank 3. Satri-cel's randomized safety read is grade >=3 TEAEs in 87 of 88 treated patients with CRS in 95% (pmid:40460847), the preclinical package missed the gastric mucosal injury patients later showed (pmid:30203099), and the one US study is closed to enrollment (nct:NCT04404595), so a ranked slot hands the PI a regimen with the worst tolerability numbers in the file and no door to reach it through. A two-patient expression match is worth a sponsor email, which the critic's own row concedes is all this is; the notes column is where it belongs.

target_intervention_label: gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel (guideline-endorsed class switch after FOLFIRINOX)
comment: I ranked this second as well, so this critique binds my own row: AGEO logged 12.5% grade 3-4 neurotoxicity in this exact post-FOLFIRINOX setting (pmid:26372701), stacking on a residual oxaliplatin neuropathy nobody has graded, and an ESMO I,B for ECOG 0-2 says nothing about a patient whose starting deficit is unknown. Of the undone workup, the CTCAE grade is the item that changes a rank rather than decorates one; at documented grade >=2 the taxane drops and the guideline slot goes with it. The missing baseline labs shift access timing across the whole board but reorder nothing.

Rank 2 is right; one of the two citations under it is not. The Groot cohort (pmid:31082915) excluded neoadjuvant-treated patients and its adjuvant therapy was gemcitabine-era, so its post-recurrence numbers do not price this patient, and the load-bearing evidence is AGEO alone (pmid:26372701): 57 patients, prospective cohort, ROBINS-I moderate, mOS 8.8 months with a 6.2-9.7 CI, a floor rather than a guarantee. The stronger support they left uncited is Tiriac's organoid work (pmid:29853643), which is the actual reason to believe FOLFIRINOX failure does not predict gem/nab-paclitaxel failure in this window.

The claim that 2+/3+ in 60% 'almost certainly' clears the 1+-pooled >=60% cutoff is arithmetic done inside the archival report: on that slide it holds by definition, but eligibility gets called on the sponsor's central assay, probably on recurrence tissue nobody has stained, with an unnamed local clone doing the conversion. Primary-to-recurrence concordance runs 83.3% and the losses cluster in local recurrence (pmid:40694660), so a value sitting exactly on the boundary has real mass on the failing side; advocate's confirm-with-the-sponsor version is closer to right. Separately, before 22.7% carries the pick, the same abstract's mOS of 9.1 months sits inside AGEO's 8.8 (95% CI 6.2-9.7, pmid:26372701) for a plain chemotherapy switch, so the ADC has not yet shown it beats the class-switch floor it would displace (doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.16_suppl.4017).

'Exactly this population' plus a high confidence label sells more than the abstract contains. RASolute 302 (pmid:42223072) enrolled patients previously treated for metastatic disease; this patient's only systemic exposure is perioperative and the recurrence is unstaged, so the allele sits inside the estimand while the clinical situation does not, and 13.2 vs 6.7 months should not be quoted as this patient's expected numbers. The rank survives on my read too, since nothing else in the file has a pre-specified RCT primary endpoint, but the transfer gap plus the 39-point-wide CI on the supporting 2L ORR (35%, 95% CI 17-56, n=26, pmid:42090791) argues moderate confidence, and I say that while working from the same abstract-level extraction they are.

target_intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) via expanded access or RASolute 303 / phase 1-2 enrollment
comment: They flagged the version gap themselves, and it should be promoted from footnote to a caveat on everything: NCCN Pancreatic v2.2026 (April 22, 2026) predates the RASolute 302 publication (pmid:42223072) and a later paywalled release could not be excluded, so every guideline-silence claim in this position is a dated snapshot, and 'no guideline names daraxonrasib' means 'none did in April' until the on-file copy is checked. Riding the pick on the trial-preferred clause rather than a category number was the defensible move; the line predicting NCCN will add the drug within a cycle or two is forecast, not evidence, and should carry no weight in the ranking. The same transfer caveat lands here as on every rank 1 including mine: the trial population was previously treated metastatic disease, which this perioperative-only, unstaged recurrence has not yet been shown to be.

I am not fighting the fallback itself; she stated no vetoes, and an ECOG 0 patient deserves a priced floor. What the rank needs is the gate made explicit: prefers_trials is true, the RASolute 303 consent clock runs 6 weeks from the metastatic diagnosis (nct:NCT07491445), so 'screening calls come first' has to mean site outreach teed up before the biopsy result lands, and no first chemo dose until the 303 and EAP (nct:NCT07573215) answers are in hand. Ranking olaparib to force the germline draw was the right advocacy, and better than my own version, which left the panel in a notes field no coordinator will read.

target_intervention_label: mKRASvax + balstilimab + botensilimab (mutant-KRAS peptide vaccine with dual checkpoint blockade)
comment: Our top four barely differ, so I am aiming at rank 5: the posted prior-therapy clause wants 4 to 6 months of first-line treatment for metastatic disease, her only exposure is perioperative, and the on-treatment biopsy runs into the vascular invasion you flagged yourself (nct:NCT06411691), so a rank tells her Baltimore is reachable while your own notes call it a warm phone line to keep for later. Nowhere in your row does the germline panel get sent, and that blood draw gates the one FDA-labeled biomarker route in this disease (pmid:31157963); NCCN has asked for it in every PDAC patient since 2019, so skipping it is a dropped ask, not triage. Your qualified on my daraxonrasib confidence lands, and I will take it: moderate is the honest label for an unstaged recurrence with perioperative-only exposure.

To a patient who said trials are welcome and travel is fine, a rank in this table reads as a door someone can call, and satri-cel has no door: the North American study stopped enrolling (nct:NCT04404595), the label is gastric and dispensed only in mainland China, and the only published contact is a PR inbox, which you yourself filed under sponsor question rather than plan. Design strength belongs in the evidence discussion, not the ranking; put the CARsgen email in notes, where risktaker and I both left it. Your IBI343 objection scores a half-hit on me: the pooled-tier arithmetic actually favors her, since 60% at 2+/3+ cannot score below 60% at >=1+ on the same block, but the unnamed clone and the never-stained recurrence are real gaps, which is why my rank 2 already gates any travel on sponsor confirmation and a re-stain.

target_intervention_label: gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel (guideline-endorsed class switch after FOLFIRINOX)
comment: You priced the trap better than any guideline page does, chemo quietly closes RASolute 303, and then ranked the regimen that springs it second with no gate attached; with prefers_trials true and the 303 consent clock starting at the metastatic diagnosis (nct:NCT07491445), rank 2 needs the same trial-preferred clause you leaned on at rank 1 written into it, screening calls resolved before any first dose. Two items she asked to keep in scope are missing from your row outright: KMT2C, where the honest line is no clinical route and two cross-tumor preclinical hypotheses at most (purine-synthesis synthetic lethality; PARPi sensitivity through HR disruption), and the MSS/TMB-low negative that forecloses checkpoint monotherapy; guideline silence is a reason to say so out loud, not to drop the line item. Your live version check on the NCCN text was the most careful sourcing this round, which is exactly why the missing accounting stands out.

Endorse, and the two gates deserve defending as guideline work rather than extra caution: NCCN wants suspected recurrence confirmed by imaging and/or biopsy, tumor NGS for every treatment candidate (March 2026 update), and tissue in hand before trial entry, so the EUS biopsy is the pathway itself, not a delay on the way to it. On critic's line-transfer objection, the two readings answer different questions and can both hold: NCCN's under-6-months recurrence rule counts FOLFIRINOX as spent when choosing the next regimen, RASolute 303 (nct:NCT07491445) counts only metastatic-setting therapy at the door, and carrying the RASolute 302 estimate (pmid:42223072) to a less pretreated patient errs in the forgiving direction, which leaves staging rather than line arithmetic as the live gate. One update to my own round-1 caveat: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v3.2026 has now posted, superseding the v2.2026 I audited, and since I cannot open it from outside the paywall, someone with access should read it before the PI repeats 'no guideline names daraxonrasib' as current.

I share the rank-1 call, so this aims at rank 4 instead. JAB-30355 (nct:NCT06386146) appears in no NCCN, ESMO, or ASCO text and its efficacy record is one sponsor sentence, which makes the rank an open door and nothing more; meanwhile this is the only position on the board that never mentions the germline panel, an NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma requirement for every confirmed PDAC patient since 2019 and the gate on the one FDA-labeled option in this file with a randomized base (POLO, pmid:31157963). A zero-data trial slot outranking an unmet guideline mandate is a compliance gap, not a difference in taste.

target_intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236, pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor) via RASolute 303, the phase 1/2, or the FDA-authorized expanded-access programme
comment: Same rank-1, but 'high' confidence claims more than an unlisted drug can carry: no NCCN, ESMO, or ASCO text names daraxonrasib as of my audit (the current posting is now v3.2026, unread behind the paywall), so the pick stands on the trial-preferred clause plus a staging call nobody has made yet. The slate underneath worries me more: all five picks are trial doors, several close together on a locally-recurrent read, and the one regimen NCCN, ESMO, and ASCO all list for this sequence, gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (ESMO Express Update 2025, grade I,B; AGEO cohort pmid:26372701), appears nowhere, so a string of screen failures leaves this patient outside every guideline page at once. Credit for sending the germline panel in the notes, but a notes line ranks nothing and olaparib is absent from the slate.

This targets rank 3, not the rank-1 we agree on, because rank 3 is where guideline silence gets misread. Silence on CLDN18.2 in PDAC (NCCN's only CLDN18.2 text sits in Gastric Cancer v3.2026, at the 75% zolbetuximab cutoff) does not forbid working the target; it routes you to a trial, which is what makes IBI343 via nct:NCT05458219 defensible and satri-cel not, since nct:NCT04404595 is closed to enrollment and the NMPA label is gastric, dispensed only in China. A rank turns CT041-ST-01's design strength (pmid:40460847) into a recommendation with no reachable route, and risktaker and advocate read the same two-patient PDAC letter and correctly left it in their notes.
